itens.descricao: JPMorgan Global Select Equity ETF (JGLO) Adds Microsoft and NXP on Oct. 29 Yahoo Finance
trechos: JPMorgan Global Select Equity ETF (JGLO) added to 10 positions and trimmed 7 on Thursday, with gross ETF activity of $122.6 million against $6.19 billion in assets.
The fund was a net seller of $33.0 million, as $22.0 million of Alphabet and $21.0 million of Apple sales outweighed its largest purchase, $18.9 million of Microsoft.
Its largest buys by dollar value were MSFT ($18.9 million), NXPI ($6.6 million) and META ($6.4 million).
Its largest sells by dollar value were GOOGL ($22.0 million), AAPL ($21.0 million) and TSM ($16.2 million).
Microsoft led the buys at $18.9 million, lifting its weight to 8.15%, followed by $6.6 million of NXP Semiconductors and $6.4 million of Meta Platforms.
AutoZone drew $2.9 million and Lowe's $2.3 million.

On the sell side, Alphabet's $22.0 million reduction left a 3.95% weight and Apple's $21.0 million cut left 4.52%, with $16.2 million of Taiwan Semiconductor, $6.1 million of Bank of America and $5.6 million of Charles Schwab also trimmed.
JPMorgan Global Select Equity ETF (JGLO) is an Equity Global fund holding 59 stocks, with 47.0% of assets in its 10 largest holdings.

itens.titulo: Chevron reports net income of $9.9bn in Q3 2026
itens.descricao: Chevron reports net income of $9.9bn in Q3 2026 Yahoo Finance
trechos: Chevron has reported net income of $9.92bn for the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026), a 180.4% increase from $3.54bn in the same period of 2025.
Total revenues and other income rose 36.4% year-on-year to $67.8bn, compared to $49.7bn a year earlier.
Reported earnings per diluted share rose by approximately 178% year-over-year, increasing from $1.82 to $5.06.
Adjusted earnings for the quarter surged by about 189%, reaching $10.4bn compared to $3.6bn in the same period last year.
Cash flow from operations (CFFO) grew by roughly 70%, climbing from $9.4bn a year ago to $16bn in the current quarter.
Chevron said the Q3 2026 results were driven by stronger margins on refined products and increased crude oil prices, although rising prices led to some negative timing impacts.
Capital expenditures in the third quarter of 2026 were lower year-on-year, largely due to decreased spending in the Permian Basin.
Segment-wise, upstream earnings increased to $5.7bn from $3.3bn a year earlier, while downstream earnings rose to $4.9bn from $1.1bn in the previous year.
